title: Celebrating the People Behind the Package
summary: Before you packed your lunch for work, fed your pet breakfast or unpacked your new kitchen appliance, a Sonoco production line was already running somewhere in the world. Perhaps a machine was repaired, or a process was improved.
body_markdown:
Before you packed your lunch for work, fed your pet breakfast or unpacked your new kitchen appliance, a Sonoco production line was already running somewhere in the world. Perhaps a machine was repaired, or a process was improved.


During this Manufacturing Month, we’re celebrating the people who help create, develop and produce Sonoco packaging. Meet three production team members who reflect the innovation, teamwork and dedication that have defined and shaped Sonoco for more than 126 years: Frankie Valle, Bryan Barrett and Paulo Almeida.


Few have witnessed Sonoco’s evolution as long as Frankie Valle, one of the longest serving production team members at the company. Beginning his career at the Hartsville, South Carolina headquarters in 1983, he has worked across various Industrial Paper departments and today serves in a maintenance planning role where he helps keep critical equipment operating efficiently and reliably.


For Valle, his manufacturing work has always been about creating solutions that people rely on each day. "I enjoy making products that people actually need and use," he shared. "It truly gives my work a sense of purpose."


His work also provides a sense of security and the opportunity to make a real difference. Since starting in his maintenance planner role, he and his team have searched for a better solution to solving leakage and wear issues on the Hartsville biomass boiler. After experimenting with various materials, they discovered a modular approach that requires less time and spend on equipment maintenance.


For his part, Valle said, “By making steam, maintaining electricity, decreasing energy costs and usage and finding ways to operate more efficiently, I’m able to help prevent cost increases for customers and improve products that people will always need.”


His enthusiasm for manufacturing at Sonoco is also rooted in the people he works alongside. "For generations, I still see the same people and families here. My father-in-law worked here and now my son does too," he shared.


And, for Valle, he is confident his team will always deliver. "You know people will stand behind you, support you and help you correct any problems that surface. That’s what makes this place so special."


Looking to the future, Valle finds both the digital transformation across manufacturing and team members embracing these tools inspiring. "This younger generation has found ways to improve products and work safely, and it's encouraging to see them accept this responsibility," Valle said. This can-do attitude makes him feel confident about the future.


After completing Sonoco’s Emerging Leaders Program, Bryan Barrett served in various manufacturing and leadership roles across the company’s Industrial Packaging business. Today, he leads operations in Newport, Tennessee, working alongside a talented team with diverse skills.


Barrett finds manufacturing rewarding, because 'no two days are the same.’ "Manufacturing processes are very repeatable, but the challenges we take on are never the same," he said. "There's always a new challenge to work on, solve, improve or go after."


This continuous improvement mindset demonstrates Sonoco's culture of innovation. Whether trying to resolve output, throughput, workforce or other challenges, he believes success starts with building strong teams and empowering people to do their best work.


"As a leader, my role is to trust the team to do the job, believe in their skills, give them the resources they need and remove roadblocks," Barrett said.


After all, mentorship and collaboration have played a significant role in his career and professional development. "From day one, Sonoco has provided me with meaningful relationships. They've been fantastic learning experiences and one of the biggest joys of my career,” he said.


When he reflects on his career thus far, one of his biggest accomplishments personally has been helping implement the Sonoco Performance System and strengthening workplace culture while serving at a Hartsville, SC operation. This effort not only drove continuous improvement but also influenced practices and team pride across other facilities.


Perhaps the most exciting changes at Sonoco are being driven by the next generation of employees. He shared, "They have new, innovative ideas on how to use technology to make a meaningful impact." Barrett shares examples of a team member who used AI to predict failures before a vibration analysis and another who created dashboards to keep the team at the forefront of KPIs.


Paired with Sonoco’s manufacturing expertise and executive leadership’s willingness to empower people to execute ideas, their work is invaluable to solving problems, keeping people safe and operating more efficiently. He said, “It’s been super rewarding to be part of the Industrial team’s pioneering efforts. I’m proud to see how our work at the plant-level pays off in big wins for the business.”


Serving in the Consumer Packaging operations in Alcochete, Portugal, Paulo Almeida shares a great sense of purpose and passion for manufacturing. After joining Sonoco as a line operator and later rejoining the company as a line mechanic, seeing the direct connection between his work and the products people use every day motivates him. "I am proud to be part of making products that are used by people around the world in their everyday lives,” he said.


Almeida revels in the challenges and opportunities that manufacturing work often presents. "It's very rewarding to solve a problem and see the final product at the end of the day," he stated.


Almeida is also passionate about Sonoco’s safety culture, which he believes has remained a high priority for everyone throughout his time at the company. "Safety is something that we are always working to improve, because we all want to go home in the same condition we came to work in,” he said.


He finds opportunities to learn, process improvement and technology advancement a source of inspiration.


Recently, he had the opportunity to assemble and implement a new production line in Portugal with state-of-the-art technology, during which he enjoyed working alongside technicians from different countries and backgrounds. “I learned a great deal about a new process and a new product. It was great to see it all come together,” he shared.


Seeing Sonoco’s collaborative spirit in action excites Almeida about the future of manufacturing. He said, “There’s always something we can learn from each other. I’m excited to see how new ideas, approaches and perspectives can help us find better ways to do things.”


As is evident, behind every Sonoco metric, process and production line is a team of individuals whose innovative spirit, dedication and collaboration makes every solution possible. Whether a veteran team member, a leader empowering colleagues to achieve new levels of success or a technician collaborating across cultures, Sonoco recognizes the foundation of success: the talented people who serve the company’s global operations each day. It is their efforts that power Sonoco today and position the company for future success.
